'''Leonid Iosifovich Vainerman''' ([[Ukrainian language|Ukrainian]]: Леонiд Йосипович Вайнерман; [[Russian language|Russian]]: Леонид Иосифович Вайнерман; alternative spelling: Leonid Iosifovich Vaynerman; born November 15, 1946, in [[Kyiv]], Ukraine) is a Ukrainian and French mathematician, professor emeritus at [[University of Caen Normandy]].<ref name="page">{{cite web | url = https://vainerman.users.lmno.cnrs.fr/ | language = fr | title = Leonid Vainerman - personal page | publisher = The French National Centre (CNRS) | access-date = September 10, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.mathsociety.kiev.ua/members/pages/03_V/Vainerman_L/index.html | title = Leonid Iosifovich Vainerman | publisher = Kyiv Mathematical Society| language = uk| access-date = September 10, 2023}}</ref> Vainerman's research results are in [[functional analysis]], [[ordinary differential equations]], [[operator theory]], [[topological groups]], [[Lie groups]], and [[abstract harmonic analysis]].<ref name="mathscinet"/> In the 1970s, he co-developed  [[Pontryagin duality#Dualities for non-commutative topological groups|Pontryagin-style dualities for non-commutative topological groups]], a set of results that served as a precursor for the modern theory of [[quantum groups]].<ref name="connes"/><ref name="book"/>

== Education and career ==

=== Degrees and appointments in Ukraine ===
Vainerman studied mathematics at the [[Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv]] and graduated in 1969. He completed his [[Ph.D.]] ([[Candidate of Sciences]] in the [[USSR]]) in 1974 at [[NASU Institute of Mathematics|Institute of Mathematics of National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]] under the direction of [[Myroslav Horbachuk]] (Gorbachuk).<ref name="mgp">{{cite web| url = https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=129343 | title = Leonid Iosifovich Vainerman | publisher = Mathematics Genealogy Project | access-date = September 10, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Vainerman | first1=Leonid I.
| last2=Gorbachuk | first2=Myroslav L.
| title=On boundary value problems for a second-order differential equation of hyperbolic type in a Hilbert space
| zbl=0318.35057
| journal=Soviet Mathematics Doklady
| volume=16
| pages=401–405
| year=1975 }}</ref> Vainerman was a professor at  [[Taras Shevchenko National University of Kyiv]]<ref>{{cite journal
| author1 = Vajnerman, L. I. | author2 = Kalyuzhnyj, A. A. 
| title = Quantized hypercomplex systems 
| zbl = 0842.46033 
| journal = Sel. Math. | volume = 13 | issue = 3 | pages = 267–281 
| year = 1994}}</ref><ref>{{cite book
| last1=Vainerman | first1=Leonid I.
| last2=Filimonova| first2=Natalya B.
| editor-first1=A. Evan
| editor-last1=Iverson
| date=July 8, 1994
| title=Algorithms for Multispectral and Hyperspectral Imagery
| chapter=Hyperspectral imagery with the application of Krawtchouk polynomials
| series=Proceedings of the SPIE
| volume=2231
| pages=148–155
| doi=10.1117/12.179775| s2cid=123625669
}}</ref> until 1992. He was a professor at [[International Solomon University]] from 1992 to 2002.<ref name="qhyper"/><ref>{{cite web| url = https://zn.ua/EDUCATION/mezhdunarodnyy_solomonov_universitet_vozrozhdenie_evreyskoy_tsivilizatsii.html | title =  International Solomon University: Renassaince of Jewish Culture | website = zn.ua | language = uk | date =  October 24, 1994}}</ref>

=== Visiting France, Belgium and Germany ===
* From 1992 to 1995, Vainerman was a visiting researcher at [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] (Paris VI). During this appointment, he had fruitful collaborations with [[Michel Enock]]<ref>{{cite journal| last1 = Enock | first1 = Michel | last2 = Vainerman | first2 = Leonid | title = Deformation of a Kac algebra by an abelian subgroup | zbl = 0876.46042 | journal = Commun. Math. Phys. | volume = 178 | issue = 3 | pages = 571–596 | year = 1996| doi = 10.1007/BF02108816 | bibcode = 1996CMaPh.178..571E | s2cid = 119863987 | url = http://projecteuclid.org/euclid.cmp/1104286767 | url-access = subscription }}</ref> and [[Richard Kerner]].<ref>{{cite journal | author1 = Vainerman, L. | author2 = Kerner, R. | title = On special classes of n-algebras | zbl = 0864.17002 | journal = J. Math. Phys. | volume = 37 | issue = 5 | pages = 2553–2565 | year = 1996| doi = 10.1063/1.531526 | bibcode = 1996JMP....37.2553V }}</ref>
* In 1999, Vainerman was a visiting researcher at [[Katholieke Universiteit Leuven]], where he had a fruitful collaboration with [[Stefaan Vaes]].<ref name="VaesVainerman2003"/>
* From 1998 to 2002, Vainerman was a visiting researcher at [[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics]] in [[Bonn]], Germany.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/preprints?year=&number=&name=Vainerman&title= | publisher = Max Planck Institute for Mathematics | title = Preprints by Leonid Vainerman | access-date = September 24, 2023}}</ref> 
* From 2000 to 2002, Vainerman was a visiting professor at the [[University of Strasbourg]] in France, where he organized a prominent meeting of theoretical physicists and mathematicians.<ref name="edited"/> While there, he also collaborated with Dmitri Nikshych and [[Vladimir Turaev]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Nikshych | first1 = Dmitri | last2 = Turaev | first2 = Vladimir | last3 = Vainerman | first3 = Leonid | title = Invariants of knots and 3-manifolds from quantum groupoids | zbl = 1021.16026 | journal = Topology Appl. | volume = 127 | issue = 1–2 | pages = 91–123 | year = 2003| doi = 10.1016/S0166-8641(02)00055-X | s2cid = 16661718 | doi-access = free | arxiv = math/0006078 }}</ref>

=== Permanent appointment in Caen ===
Vainerman joined the [[University of Caen Normandy]] as an associate professor in [[Nicolas Oresme]] Mathematics Laboratory,<ref name="research"/> becoming a full professor in 2005. He directed three Ph.D. dissertations there (those of Pierre Fima, Camille Mével and Frank Taipe).<ref name="mgp"/><ref>{{cite web| url = https://theses.fr/fr/085548537 | title = Leonid Vainerman | publisher = ABES search engine for French doctoral theses (theses.fr) | access-date = September 10, 2023}}</ref> He has been a professor emeritus at [[University of Caen Normandy]] since 2015.<ref name="page"/> While at Caen, Vainerman collaborated with Dmitri Nikshych<ref name = "finite_groupoids"/> and [[Jean-Michel Vallin]].<ref name="weak_hopf"/>

== Scientific contributions ==

In the 1970s, Vainerman collaborated with George I. Kac (Georgii Isaakovich Kac)<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Vainerman | first1=Leonid I.
| last2=Kats| first2=George I.
| title=Nonunimodular ring groups and Hopf–von Neumann algebras
| journal=Doklady Akademii Nauk SSSR
| volume=211
| issue=5
| year=1973
| pages=1031–1034
| zbl=0296.46072
| url=https://www.mathnet.ru/php/archive.phtml?wshow=paper&jrnid=dan&paperid=37841&option_lang=eng}}</ref> on generalizations of [[Pontryagin duality]] to non-commutative groups and developed the concept now known as Kac algebras<ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Berezanskii | first1=Yu. M. 
| last2=Berezin | first2=F. A.
| last3=Bogolyubov | first3=N. N.
| last4=Vainerman | first4=L. I.
| last5=Daletskii | first5=Yu. L.
| last6=Kirillov | first6=A. A.
| last7=Palyutkin | first7=V. G.
| last8=Khatset | first8=B. I.
| last9=Èidel'man | first9=S. D.
| title=Georgii Isaakovich Kac (obituary)
| journal=Russian Mathematical Surveys
| volume=34
| issue=2
| date=1979
| pages=213–217
| doi=10.1070/RM1979v034n02ABEH002912| bibcode=1979RuMaS..34..213B 
| s2cid=250754802 
}}</ref><ref name="izumi book">{{cite book
| last1=Izumi | first1=Masaki
| last2=Kosaki | first2=Hideki 
| title=Kac algebras arising from composition of subfactors: General theory and classification
| zbl = 1001.46040
| series=Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society
| volume=158
| date=2002
| issue=750
| doi=10.1090/memo/0750}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal 
| last1=Vainerman | first1=Leonid
| title=Ideas that will outlast us
| zbl=1302.01050 
| journal=Newsletter of the European Mathematical Society
| volume=92
| pages=16–21 
| year=2014
| url=https://ems.press/content/serial-issue-files/13722}}</ref><ref>{{cite book 
| last1=Masuda | first1=Toshihiko
| last2=Tomatsu | first2=Reiji 
| title=Classification of actions of discrete Kac algebras on injective factors
| zbl=1376.46052
| series=Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society
| volume=245
| year=2016
| issue=1160
| doi=10.1090/memo/1160| s2cid=119321613
}}</ref> (distinct from [[Kac-Moody algebras]]).

According to the French mathematician [[Alain Connes]],<ref name="connes">{{cite book | url = https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-662-02813-1#about-this-book| first = Alain | last = Connes | title = Preface to the book 'Kac algebras' | year=1992 | publisher = Springer| doi = 10.1007/978-3-662-02813-1 | isbn = 978-3-642-08128-6 }}</ref> {{cquote|The theory of Kac algebras and their duality, [was] elaborated independently by M. Enock and J. -M. Schwartz, and by G. I. Kac and L. I. Vainermann in the seventies. The subject has now reached a state of maturity }}
The two teams independently developed a general [[Pontryagin duality]] theory for all [[locally compact group]]s. The contributions of both teams are covered in the 1992 book by [[Michel Enock]] and Jean-Marie Schwartz on Kac algebras.<ref name="book">{{cite book |last1=Enock|first1=Michel|last2=Schwartz|first2=Jean-Marie|title=Kac Algebras and Duality of Locally Compact Groups|year=1992|publisher=Springer-Verlag|isbn=978-3-540-54745-7| others=With a preface by Alain Connes. With a postface by Adrian Ocneanu| location= Berlin|mr=1215933|doi=10.1007/978-3-662-02813-1}}</ref> Per Alain Connes,<ref name="connes"/> these results form "a general theory to characterize [[quantum groups]] among [[Hopf algebras]], similar to the characterization of [[Lie groups]] among [[locally compact group]]s." As mentioned in the postface by {{ill|Adrian Ocneanu|de}} to the book by Enock and Schwartz,<ref name="book"/> Kac algebras and their actions on [[von Neumann algebra]]s naturally arise in the theory of [[subfactor]]s developed by [[Vaughan Jones]].<ref name="izumi book"/><ref>{{cite journal
| last1=Izumi | first1=Masaki
| last2=Longo | first2=Roberto
| last3=Popa | first3=Sorin | authorlink3=Sorin Popa
| title=A Galois correspondence for compact groups of automorphisms of von Neumann algebras with a generalization to Kac algebras
| zbl=0915.46051
| journal=Journal of Functional Analysis
| volume=155
| issue=1
| pages=25–63 
| date=1998
| doi=10.1006/jfan.1997.3228 | doi-access=free| arxiv=funct-an/9604004
}}</ref>

In his subsequent research, Vainerman obtained results on [[C*-algebras]], [[Hopf algebras]] and [[quantum groups]], as well as quantum [[hypergroup]]s and [[quantum groupoid]]s.<ref name="qhyper">{{cite journal

| url=https://www.theta.ro/jot/archive/1999-041-002/1999-041-002-002.pdf}}
</ref><ref name = "finite_groupoids">{{cite book

}}</ref><ref name="VaesVainerman2003">{{cite journal

| zbl=1034.46068
| journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]]
| volume=175
| issue=1
| pages=1–101
| date=2003
| doi=10.1016/S0001-8708(02)00040-3 | doi-access=free| arxiv=math/0101133
}}
</ref><ref name="weak_hopf">{{cite journal
| last1=Vainerman | first1=Leonid
| last2=Vallin | first2=Jean-Michel 
| title=Classifying (weak) coideal subalgebras of weak Hopf <math>C^*</math>-algebras
| zbl=1446.16037
| journal=Journal of Algebra
| volume=550
| pages=333–357
| date=2020
| doi=10.1016/j.jalgebra.2019.12.026| doi-access=free
| arxiv=1904.07602
}}
</ref> Vainerman's research advanced the theory of quantum groups, including structural results on C*-algebraic quantum groups and their actions on operator algebras.<ref name="VaesVainerman2003" /> He has made notable contributions to the structure and classification of weak Hopf C*-algebras (sometimes described as quantum groupoids), with applications to topics such as subfactors, dynamical quantum groups, and the construction of [[knot invariants]] and [[3-manifolds]].<ref name="finite_groupoids" /><ref name="weak_hopf" /> His collaborative works include surveys and original research articles detailing the foundational theory and applications of finite quantum groupoids.<ref name = "finite_groupoids"/> 

Vainerman is credited as a co-author or editor in more than 70 mathematics publications.<ref name="mathscinet
">{{cite web | url = https://mathscinet.ams.org/mathscinet/MRAuthorID/191849 | title = Publication of Leonid I. Vainerman | publisher = [[MathSciNet]] | access-date = September 10, 2023}}</ref><ref name="research">{{cite web| url = https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Leonid-Vainerman | title = Leonid Vainerman | access-date = September 10, 2023}}</ref>

== Scientific leadership ==

Vainerman organized a meeting at the [[University of Strasbourg]] February 21–23, 2002 that assembled theoretical physicists and mathematicians specializing in [[quantum group]] and [[quantum groupoid]] applications in quantum theories beyond the [[Standard Model]]. Vainerman edited the proceedings of the meeting and had them published as a book in 2003.<ref name="edited">{{cite book|editor-first=Leonid|editor-last=Vainerman|title=Locally Compact Quantum Groups and Groupoids: Proceedings of the Meeting of Theoretical Physicists and Mathematicians, Strasbourg, February 21–23, 2002|series = IRMA Lectures in Mathematics and Theoretical Physics. 2 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=0ecjM-nPhGcC|access-date=September 10, 2023|year=2003|publisher=Walter de Gruyter|isbn=978-3-11-020005-8|pages=247|zbl = 1005.00029}}</ref>
